pull.title: KAFKA-21214: [8/8] Add the uniform2 consumer group assignor
pull.body:
The uniform assignor balances the total number of partitions per member
but not the partitions of each topic: with homogeneous subscriptions, a
member can get all the partitions of a topic while the others get none
of them. The throughput is usually about the same across the partitions
of a topic but not across topics, so adding members does not spread the
load.

This patch adds uniform2, the next version of the uniform assignor, from
the steps of the previous patches. It lives next to the uniform assignor
while it is developed and is not registered as a built-in assignor. Its
assignments have these properties, in priority order:
- Every partition of every subscribed topic goes to exactly one of its
  subscribers.
- Every subscriber of a topic gets the same number of its partitions,
  the minimum quota, or one more, with an extra partition.
- No extra partition could move to another subscriber of its topic
  whose assignment is at least two partitions smaller.
- Partitions stay with their owners where the above allows. The
  placement moves the fewest partitions for the quotas, and an
  assignment that already has these properties is returned unchanged.
- The result is deterministic.

Changes:
- `Uniform2Assignor` and `AssignmentBuilder`, which reads the group,
  runs the `KeepStickyExtraPartitions`, `AssignRemainingExtraPartitions`
  and `BalanceExtraPartitions` steps on the quotas, places every topic
  and builds the result. Partitions of topics that a member does not
  subscribe to or which no longer exist are dropped. The class Javadoc
  of `Uniform2Assignor` describes the steps with a worked example.
- The result reuses the maps and sets of the members that do not change.
  `RangeSet` becomes public to return consecutive partitions.
- The assignor does not use racks yet. Rack awareness comes in a later
  patch.
- `ConsumerAssignorBenchmark` gets `UNIFORM2`.
- End to end tests with hand traced expectations, written with the group
  spec and topics fixtures, and a shared checker of the properties.

Reviewers: Sean Quah <squah@confluent.io>

Without seeing the usage site, this concept is very strange, especially with the double counting. The natural implementation would be to return the number of subscribed topics of the member's cohort. It needs an explanation for why we don't use the natural implementation. Also maybe the naming isn't the best.

---

When each topic has more partitions than members, we will exceed the subscribed topic count most of the time.
`min(existing_expression, member's cohort's subscribed topic count)`?
but that wouldn't really help with understanding the method's purpose.

typo?
```suggestion
     * @return The largest number of partitions of a topic, or 0 if there are no subscribed topics.
```
very minor nit: the field declaration order has `nextPartition` before `membersGettingPartitions`

+    /**

+     * partition of each. T3 has a minimum quota of 1 and 2 extra partitions. A owns partitions 0

+    @Test
+    public void testAnExtraPartitionGoesToAnotherMemberWhenTheSmallestHaveOneOfTheTopic() {

+    /**
+     * A subscribes to T1, B to T1 and T3, and C and D to T2 and T4. T1 and T2, of 1 partition each

+    @Test
+    public void testCohortsWaitingForAnExtraPartitionOfOneTopicDoNotCarryOverToTheNext() {

+    /**

+    @Test
+    public void testHeterogeneousBalancesAcrossTopics() {

+    /**
+     * A subscribes to T1 and T2, B to T1 and C to T2, of 3 partitions each, so each topic has a

+    @Test
+    public void testBalanceMovesExtraPartitionsKeptByTheirOwner() {

+
+    /**
+     * A subscribes to T1, T2 and T3, B to T1 and T2, C to T2 and T3, and D to T1 and T3, in four
+     * cohorts. T1, T2 and T3, of 5 partitions each over 3 subscribers, have a minimum quota of 1
+     * and 2 extra partitions each, all kept by owners of 2 partitions: A keeps one of every topic,
+     * B one of T1 and one of T2, and C one of T3. The assignment sizes are 6, 4, 3 and 2. A gives
+     * the extra partition of T3 to D, the smallest, then the one of T2 to C. The assignment sizes

+     */
+    @Test
+    public void testBalanceMovesUntilNoExtraPartitionCanMove() {
+        var spec = new GroupSpecFixture()
+            .withMember("A", Set.of(T1, T2, T3), Map.of(T1, Set.of(0, 1), T2, Set.of(0, 1), T3, Set.of(0, 1)))

+            "D", Map.of(T1, Set.of(4), T3, Set.of(1, 4))

+
+    /**
+     * A subscribes to T1 and T4, and B and C to T1, T2 and T3. T1, of 5 partitions over the three,

+    /**
+     * A and C subscribe to T1 to T4, and B to T1 to T5. T1 to T4, of 4 partitions over the three,

commit.message:
KAFKA-21214: [8/8] Add the uniform2 consumer group assignor

The uniform assignor balances the total number of partitions per member
but not the partitions of each topic: with homogeneous subscriptions, a
member can get all the partitions of a topic while the others get none
of them. The throughput is usually about the same across the partitions
of a topic but not across topics, so adding members does not spread the
load.

This patch adds uniform2, the next version of the uniform assignor, from
the steps of the previous patches. It lives next to the uniform assignor
while it is developed and is not registered as a built-in assignor. Its
assignments have these properties, in priority order:
- Every partition of every subscribed topic goes to exactly one of its
  subscribers.
- Every subscriber of a topic gets the same number of its partitions,
  the minimum quota, or one more, with an extra partition.
- No extra partition could move to another subscriber of its topic
  whose assignment is at least two partitions smaller.
- Partitions stay with their owners where the above allows. The
  placement moves the fewest partitions for the quotas, and an
  assignment that already has these properties is returned unchanged.
- The result is deterministic.

Changes:
- `Uniform2Assignor` and `AssignmentBuilder`, which reads the group,
  runs the `KeepStickyExtraPartitions`, `AssignRemainingExtraPartitions`
  and `BalanceExtraPartitions` steps on the quotas, places every topic
  and builds the result. Partitions of topics that a member does not
  subscribe to or which no longer exist are dropped. The class Javadoc
  of `Uniform2Assignor` describes the steps with a worked example.
- The result reuses the maps and sets of the members that do not change.
  `RangeSet` becomes public to return consecutive partitions.
  `Quotas.maxTopicsWithPartitions` bounds the size of the new maps.
- The assignor does not use racks yet. Rack awareness comes in a later
  patch.
- `ConsumerAssignorBenchmark` gets `UNIFORM2`.
- End to end tests with hand traced expectations, written with the group
  spec and topics fixtures, and a shared checker of the properties.

+

+            "B", Map.of(T1, Set.of(1), T2, Set.of(2), T3, Set.of(2, 3, 4)),
+            "C", Map.of(T2, Set.of(3, 4), T3, Set.of(5, 6))
+        ), result);
+    }
+
+    @ParameterizedTest
+    @EnumSource(SubscriptionType.class)
+    public void testAssignmentReuse(SubscriptionType subscriptionType) {
+        CommonAssignorTests.testAssignmentReuse(assignor, subscriptionType, false);
+    }
+
+    @ParameterizedTest
+    @EnumSource(SubscriptionType.class)
+    public void testReassignmentStickiness(SubscriptionType subscriptionType) {
+        CommonAssignorTests.testReassignmentStickiness(assignor, subscriptionType, false);
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * The assignment does not depend on the order of the members, of the topics of their

+     * also checked by {@link #testReassignmentStickiness}; this test also shuffles the topics of
+     * the subscriptions and the entries of the current assignments.

+    @Test
+    public void testOrderIndependence() {
+        var describer = new TopicsFixture()
+            .withTopic(T1, 2)
+            .withTopic(T2, 5)
+            .withTopic(T3, 7)
+            .build();
+        var forward = new GroupSpecFixture()
+            .withMember("A", new LinkedHashSet<>(List.of(T1, T2, T3)), Map.of(T3, Set.of(0, 1, 2, 3)))
+            .withMember("B", new LinkedHashSet<>(List.of(T1, T2)))

issue.title: KAFKA-21355: Add a fuzzer for the uniform2 assignor

repository.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

issue.body:
The unit tests of the uniform2 assignor check hand traced cases, but its
properties must hold for any group and any sequence of changes.

This patch adds a fuzzer checking them on random groups and random
sequences of events: members joining and leaving, one at a time or
several, topics gaining partitions, and subscriptions changing. Other
events make the input stale, as the coordinator can pass it to the
assignor, such as topics deleted or created again while members still
hold their partitions, and empty subscriptions.

Changes:
- `Uniform2FuzzScenario` generates the groups and the events, and passes
  every group to the assignor as a group spec built with
  `GroupSpecFixture`.
- `Uniform2AssignorFuzzTest` checks validity, spread and balance,
  determinism under shuffled inputs, the fixed point with the same map
  instances, the same map for every member whose partitions do not
  change, the movement bounds after a single leave or join, and the
  moves of tiny groups, at most one above the fewest found by a brute
  force oracle.
- It also checks that the two ways of counting of the balance step give
  the same quotas, and that a run of at least 2,000 events goes through
  every kind of event.
- The default run takes seconds, and environment variables scale it up,
  see the class Javadoc.

KAFKA-21214: [8/8] Add the uniform2 consumer group assignor

The uniform assignor balances the total number of partitions per member
but not the partitions of each topic: with homogeneous subscriptions, a
member can get all the partitions of a topic while the others get none
of them. The throughput is usually about the same across the partitions
of a topic but not across topics, so adding members does not spread the
load.

This patch adds uniform2, the next version of the uniform assignor, from
the steps of the previous patches. It lives next to the uniform assignor
while it is developed and is not registered as a built-in assignor. Its
assignments have these properties, in priority order:
- Every partition of every subscribed topic goes to exactly one of its
  subscribers.
- Every subscriber of a topic gets the same number of its partitions,
  the minimum quota, or one more, with an extra partition.
- No extra partition could move to another subscriber of its topic
  whose assignment is at least two partitions smaller.
- Partitions stay with their owners where the above allows. The
  placement moves the fewest partitions for the quotas, and an
  assignment that already has these properties is returned unchanged.
- The result is deterministic.

Changes:
- `Uniform2Assignor` and `AssignmentBuilder`, which reads the group,
  runs the `KeepStickyExtraPartitions`, `AssignRemainingExtraPartitions`
  and `BalanceExtraPartitions` steps on the quotas, places every topic
  and builds the result. Partitions of topics that a member does not
  subscribe to or which no longer exist are dropped. The class Javadoc
  of `Uniform2Assignor` describes the steps with a worked example.
- The result reuses the maps and sets of the members that do not change.
  `RangeSet` becomes public to return consecutive partitions.
  `Quotas.maxTopicsWithPartitions` bounds the size of the new maps.
- The assignor does not use racks yet. Rack awareness comes in a later
  patch.
- `ConsumerAssignorBenchmark` gets `UNIFORM2`.
- End to end tests with hand traced expectations, written with the group
  spec and topics fixtures, and a shared checker of the properties.
